items.question: Omeprazole reduces gastric acid by inhibiting the?
items.explanation: Omeprazole is a proton pump inhibitor, irreversibly blocking H+/K+ ATPase in parietal cells.

items.question: Which PPI is commonly used in peptic ulcer disease?
items.explanation: Omeprazole and other PPIs provide potent, long-lasting acid suppression for peptic ulcers/GERD.

items.question: Vonoprazan suppresses acid as a?
items.explanation: Vonoprazan is a potassium-competitive acid blocker (P-CAB) giving faster, more sustained acid suppression than PPIs.

items.question: Why does long-term PPI use increase fracture and infection risk?
options: Reduced calcium/B12 absorption and altered gut flora
items.explanation: Prolonged acid suppression impairs calcium/B12 absorption and raises enteric infection (C. difficile) risk.

items.question: Vaughan-Williams class III antiarrhythmics act mainly by blocking?
items.explanation: Class III agents (amiodarone, sotalol) block K+ channels, prolonging the action potential and refractory period.

Q: Why does long-term PPI use increase fracture and infection risk?

Q: Vaughan-Williams class III antiarrhythmics act mainly by blocking?
Ans: Potassium channels (prolonging repolarisation)
